newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek diplomats, TV say tanks in Albania town.
newsitem.headline: Greek diplomats, TV say tanks in Albania town.

text.p: Tanks have been spotted in the southern Albanian town of Gjirokaster and gunfire from automatic weapons was occasionally heard on Monday, Greek diplomats and eyewitnesses said.

"At least five or six tanks are inside the town now and have taken up key positions. There has been sporadic gunfire from automatic weapons throughout the day," a Greek consulate official in Gjirokaster who requested anonymity told Reuters by telephone.
An Albanian army source in Tirana said there were tanks near Gjirokaster but did not confirm that any were actually in the town itself.
"There are tanks near the town. They are not undertaking any offensive operations. They moved a bit out of the garrison near Gjirokaster," the source said.

A state of emergency and nationwide curfew came into force throughout Albania on Monday in response to armed unrest in the south of the Balkan country. Athens television showed pictures of tanks in Gjirokaster, where protesters stole weapons from army depots, torched police stations and looted stores on Sunday and early on Monday.

"I saw the tanks come out of the north and entering Gjirokaster down the main road," said a town resident called Pavlo, also contacted by telephone. "The streets are empty now because there is a curfew after eight in the evening (1900 GMT)."
